functional_semantics.triton: y = x * (1/sqrt(sum x^2 + eps)) per row, fp32 statistics, cast back to x dtype (impl_triton.py:22-35).
functional_semantics.cutile: y = x * rsqrt(sum x^2 + eps) per row, fp32, cast back (impl_cutile.py:28-49).
functional_semantics.note: Both match impl_torch.py:5-7 (vector_norm in fp32, squared, rsqrt(norm_sq + eps), cast). Generator tensors.py:461-463 returns (x, eps) with eps from case_defaults.

stages.triton: reshape view (impl_triton.py:53-55), empty_like (56), one launch grid (M,) (60-77), return reshape view (78).
stages.cutile: reshape view (impl_cutile.py:61), empty_like (62-63), one launch grid (batch_M,1,1) (85-87).
stages.note: Both fuse statistics and apply in one kernel with one program per row.

dependencies.triton: pass 2 depends on rstd from pass 1 of the same row (impl_triton.py:27,34).
dependencies.cutile: pass 2 depends on rstd from pass 1 (impl_cutile.py:38,48).

reduction_scan_sort.triton: lane-wise fp32 accumulation over chunks then one tl.sum (impl_triton.py:22-27).
reduction_scan_sort.cutile: lane-wise fp32 accumulation over tiles then one ct.sum (impl_cutile.py:28-38).
reduction_scan_sort.note: Same structure; row re-read in pass 2 on both sides (impl_triton.py:30-35, impl_cutile.py:41-49).

precision.triton: fp32 upcast on load, fp32 acc, rstd = 1/tl.sqrt(...) fp32, explicit cast to X dtype at store (impl_triton.py:25-27,33-35).
precision.cutile: fp32 upcast, fp32 acc, ct.rsqrt fp32, ct.astype to x.dtype (impl_cutile.py:30-38,42-48).
precision.note: 1/sqrt vs rsqrt intrinsic is a primitive choice within tolerance; contract permits either.

preprocessing.triton: reshape (view) + contiguous only if inner stride != 1 (impl_triton.py:53-55).
preprocessing.note: Both are views for the generator's contiguous inputs; nothing cached; output allocated per call.

hardware_dispatch.triton: no dispatch branches; row length is a constexpr (impl_triton.py:13).
hardware_dispatch.cutile: no dispatch branches; row length is ConstInt (impl_cutile.py:23).
hardware_dispatch.note: Compile-time row length on both sides is an audit observation, not a contract requirement.

fq_boundary.note: Compulsory-traffic model: X read once + Y written once. Both implementations re-read each row in the apply pass, so the formula is a lower bound on issued traffic (the second read is partly L2-served). Nothing is untimed or prepacked; the view/alloc are inside run(). Convention differs from layernorm's config, which counts the re-read (3n); the contract pins neither.
